answer.summary: For a one-sample t-test comparing the mean of a normally distributed outcome against a null mean of 0, with a hypothesized mean increase of 0.2 units, population SD of 0.5 units, one-sided alternative (μ > 0), significance level α = 0.05, and target power of 80%, the minimum integer sample size is **41 participants**. This design achieves an actual power of 80.86%, while n=40 yields 79.97% power (below target). The effect size (Cohen's d = 0.4) and sample size were determined via binary search over the exact non-central t-distribution.
answer.method: Sample-size inversion via binary search using the exact non-central t-distribution. For each candidate sample size n, the non-centrality parameter is computed as ncp = d√n where d = 0.4 (Cohen's d), and power is calculated as P(T > t_{crit} | H₁) where t_{crit} = t_{1−α}(n−1) is the critical value for a one-sided test. The search identified the smallest integer n where power ≥ 80%.
assumptions: Outcome follows a normal distribution with constant population SD = 0.5 units
One-sample test against a null mean of 0
Type I error rate (two-tailed significance level) α = 0.05
Type II error rate β = 0.20 (target power = 1 − β = 0.80)
No missing data or violations of distributional assumptions
Effect size (mean difference) δ = 0.2 units is fixed
limitations: Sample-size planning assumes the true effect size equals the hypothesized value; underpowered if the true effect is smaller than 0.2 units
Power calculation assumes a balanced, complete case scenario with no attrition
Exact power depends on achieving the specified effect size and population variance in practice
The calculation is valid only under the stated normal-theory assumptions; robustness to departures from normality depends on sample size and tail behavior
No correction for multiple testing or interim analyses

# One-sample t-test sample size calculation
# H0: μ = 0 vs H1: μ > 0 (one-sided)
# Effect: mean_diff = 0.2, SD = 0.5
# Alpha = 0.05, Target power = 0.80

# Parameters
mean_diff <- 0.2
sd <- 0.5
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80
cohens_d <- mean_diff / sd

cat("Study Parameters:\n")
cat("Mean difference (δ):", mean_diff, "\n")
cat("Standard deviation (σ):", sd, "\n")
cat("Cohen's d:", cohens_d, "\n")
cat("Alpha (one-sided):", alpha, "\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n\n")

# Function to compute power for one-sample t-test
# n: sample size
# d: Cohen's d effect size
# alpha: significance level (one-sided)
power_one_sample_t <- function(n, d, alpha) {
  # Non-centrality parameter
  ncp <- d * sqrt(n)
  
  # Critical value for one-sided test
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df = n - 1)
  
  # Power: P(T > t_crit | H1)
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df = n - 1, ncp = ncp)
  
  return(power)
}

# Test the function with a few sample sizes
test_ns <- c(20, 25, 30)
cat("Initial power exploration:\n")
for (n in test_ns) {
  p <- power_one_sample_t(n, cohens_d, alpha)
  cat("n =", n, ": power =", round(p, 4), "\n")
}
cat("\n")

# Binary search for minimum n achieving target power
n_low <- 2
n_high <- 1000

while (n_high - n_low > 1) {
  n_mid <- floor((n_low + n_high) / 2)
  power_mid <- power_one_sample_t(n_mid, cohens_d, alpha)
  
  if (power_mid >= target_power) {
    n_high <- n_mid
  } else {
    n_low <- n_mid
  }
}

n_min <- n_high
power_min <- power_one_sample_t(n_min, cohens_d, alpha)
power_prev <- power_one_sample_t(n_min - 1, cohens_d, alpha)

cat("Sample Size Inversion Results:\n")
cat("Minimum n achieving 80% power:", n_min, "participants\n")
cat("Power at n =", n_min, ":", round(power_min, 6), "\n")
cat("Power at n =", n_min - 1, ":", round(power_prev, 6), "\n\n")

# Verify calculation with closed-form approximation
# For reference: Wallis (2009) approximation for one-sample t-test
# n ≈ (z_{1-α} + z_{1-β})^2 / d^2 + d^2 / 4
z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha)  # one-sided
z_beta <- qnorm(target_power)
n_approx_wallis <- (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 / cohens_d^2 + cohens_d^2 / 4

cat("Closed-form approximation (Wallis):\n")
cat("n_approx ≈", round(n_approx_wallis, 2), "\n\n")

# Output for submission
cat("FINAL ANSWER:\n")
cat("Minimum integer sample size: n =", n_min, "participants\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", n_min, ":", round(power_min, 6), "\n")

# Emit structured result
results <- list(
  metric = "sample_size",
  value = n_min,
  unit = "participants_total"
)

library(jsonlite)
cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(toJSON(list(results = list(results)), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))
cat("\n")

# Independent verification of one-sample t-test sample-size calculation
# Using base R and alternative methodology to validate the candidate's answer

# Parameters
delta <- 0.2  # mean difference
sigma <- 0.5  # population SD
cohens_d <- delta / sigma
alpha <- 0.05  # one-sided
target_power <- 0.80

cat("=== INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION ===\n\n")
cat("Study Design:\n")
cat("  Hypothesis: H0: μ = 0 vs H1: μ > 0 (one-sided)\n")
cat("  Mean difference: δ =", delta, "\n")
cat("  Population SD: σ =", sigma, "\n")
cat("  Cohen's d = δ/σ =", cohens_d, "\n")
cat("  Significance level: α =", alpha, "(one-sided)\n")
cat("  Target power: 1 - β =", target_power, "\n\n")

# Power function for one-sample t-test
# ncp = d * sqrt(n)
# Reject H0 if T > t_crit where t_crit = qt(1 - alpha, df = n - 1)
# Power = P(T > t_crit | non-centrality = ncp)

power_calc <- function(n, d, alpha) {
  if (n <= 1) return(0)
  ncp <- d * sqrt(n)
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df = n - 1)
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df = n - 1, ncp = ncp)
  return(power)
}

# Verify candidate's answers
cat("Verification of candidate's results:\n")
cat("  n = 40: power =", round(power_calc(40, cohens_d, alpha), 6), "\n")
cat("  n = 41: power =", round(power_calc(41, cohens_d, alpha), 6), "\n")
cat("  n = 42: power =", round(power_calc(42, cohens_d, alpha), 6), "\n\n")

# Systematic search to confirm minimum n
cat("Detailed search around the minimum:\n")
for (n in 38:44) {
  p <- power_calc(n, cohens_d, alpha)
  meets_target <- ifelse(p >= target_power, "✓ MEETS", "✗ below")
  cat(sprintf("  n = %2d: power = %.6f  %s\n", n, p, meets_target))
}

cat("\n")

# Confirm the minimum
n_min_candidate <- 41
power_at_min <- power_calc(n_min_candidate, cohens_d, alpha)
power_at_prev <- power_calc(n_min_candidate - 1, cohens_d, alpha)

if (power_at_prev < target_power && power_at_min >= target_power) {
  cat("✓ CONFIRMED: n =", n_min_candidate, "is the minimum integer achieving target power\n")
  cat("  Power at n = 40:", round(power_at_prev, 6), "(below 80%)\n")
  cat("  Power at n = 41:", round(power_at_min, 6), "(≥80%)\n\n")
} else {
  cat("✗ INCONSISTENCY DETECTED\n")
  cat("  Expected n - 1 to have power < 80% and n to have power ≥ 80%\n")
  cat("  Actual: power(n-1) =", round(power_at_prev, 6), 
      ", power(n) =", round(power_at_min, 6), "\n\n")
}

# Alternative check: use power.t.test if available (though it uses different assumptions)
# Note: base R's power.t.test uses a different parameterization and assumes known variance
# For comparison, we can use a normal approximation

# Normal approximation (Zα + Zβ)²/d²
z_alpha_one <- qnorm(1 - alpha)
z_beta <- qnorm(target_power)
n_normal_approx <- (z_alpha_one + z_beta)^2 / cohens_d^2

cat("Normal approximation (z-method):\n")
cat("  n ≈", round(n_normal_approx, 2), "\n")
cat("  (This is typically conservative for small n due to t-distribution)\n\n")

# Output for review
cat("=== CONCLUSION ===\n")
cat("Sample-size answer: n = 41 participants\n")
cat("Achieved power: ", round(power_at_min, 4), "\n")
cat("Method: Exact non-central t-distribution (correct approach)\n")

results <- list(
  metric = "sample_size_verification",
  value = n_min_candidate,
  unit = "participants_total",
  power_achieved = round(power_at_min, 6),
  power_at_n_minus_1 = round(power_at_prev, 6)
)

library(jsonlite)
cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(toJSON(list(results = list(results)), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

# Independent verification of one-sample t-test sample-size calculation
# Using base R and alternative methodology to validate the candidate's answer

# Parameters
delta <- 0.2  # mean difference
sigma <- 0.5  # population SD
cohens_d <- delta / sigma
alpha <- 0.05  # one-sided
target_power <- 0.80

cat("=== INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION ===\n\n")
cat("Study Design:\n")
cat("  Hypothesis: H0: μ = 0 vs H1: μ > 0 (one-sided)\n")
cat("  Mean difference: δ =", delta, "\n")
cat("  Population SD: σ =", sigma, "\n")
cat("  Cohen's d = δ/σ =", cohens_d, "\n")
cat("  Significance level: α =", alpha, "(one-sided)\n")
cat("  Target power: 1 - β =", target_power, "\n\n")

# Power function for one-sample t-test
# ncp = d * sqrt(n)
# Reject H0 if T > t_crit where t_crit = qt(1 - alpha, df = n - 1)
# Power = P(T > t_crit | non-centrality = ncp)

power_calc <- function(n, d, alpha) {
  if (n <= 1) return(0)
  ncp <- d * sqrt(n)
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df = n - 1)
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df = n - 1, ncp = ncp)
  return(power)
}

# Verify candidate's answers
cat("Verification of candidate's results:\n")
cat("  n = 40: power =", round(power_calc(40, cohens_d, alpha), 6), "\n")
cat("  n = 41: power =", round(power_calc(41, cohens_d, alpha), 6), "\n")
cat("  n = 42: power =", round(power_calc(42, cohens_d, alpha), 6), "\n\n")

# Systematic search to confirm minimum n
cat("Detailed search around the minimum:\n")
for (n in 38:44) {
  p <- power_calc(n, cohens_d, alpha)
  meets_target <- ifelse(p >= target_power, "✓ MEETS", "✗ below")
  cat(sprintf("  n = %2d: power = %.6f  %s\n", n, p, meets_target))
}

cat("\n")

# Confirm the minimum
n_min_candidate <- 41
power_at_min <- power_calc(n_min_candidate, cohens_d, alpha)
power_at_prev <- power_calc(n_min_candidate - 1, cohens_d, alpha)

if (power_at_prev < target_power && power_at_min >= target_power) {
  cat("✓ CONFIRMED: n =", n_min_candidate, "is the minimum integer achieving target power\n")
  cat("  Power at n = 40:", round(power_at_prev, 6), "(below 80%)\n")
  cat("  Power at n = 41:", round(power_at_min, 6), "(≥80%)\n\n")

}

# Evidence e1; success=true

# One-sample t-test sample size calculation
# H0: μ = 0 vs H1: μ > 0 (one-sided)
# Effect: mean_diff = 0.2, SD = 0.5
# Alpha = 0.05, Target power = 0.80

# Parameters
mean_diff <- 0.2
sd <- 0.5
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80
cohens_d <- mean_diff / sd

cat("Study Parameters:\n")
cat("Mean difference (δ):", mean_diff, "\n")
cat("Standard deviation (σ):", sd, "\n")
cat("Cohen's d:", cohens_d, "\n")
cat("Alpha (one-sided):", alpha, "\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n\n")

# Function to compute power for one-sample t-test
# n: sample size
# d: Cohen's d effect size
# alpha: significance level (one-sided)
power_one_sample_t <- function(n, d, alpha) {
  # Non-centrality parameter
  ncp <- d * sqrt(n)
  
  # Critical value for one-sided test
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df = n - 1)
  
  # Power: P(T > t_crit | H1)
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df = n - 1, ncp = ncp)
  
  return(power)
}

# Test the function with a few sample sizes
test_ns <- c(20, 25, 30)
cat("Initial power exploration:\n")
for (n in test_ns) {
  p <- power_one_sample_t(n, cohens_d, alpha)
  cat("n =", n, ": power =", round(p, 4), "\n")
}
cat("\n")

# Binary search for minimum n achieving target power
n_low <- 2
n_high <- 1000

while (n_high - n_low > 1) {
  n_mid <- floor((n_low + n_high) / 2)
  power_mid <- power_one_sample_t(n_mid, cohens_d, alpha)
  
  if (power_mid >= target_power) {
    n_high <- n_mid
  } else {
    n_low <- n_mid
  }
}

n_min <- n_high
power_min <- power_one_sample_t(n_min, cohens_d, alpha)
power_prev <- power_one_sample_t(n_min - 1, cohens_d, alpha)

cat("Sample Size Inversion Results:\n")
cat("Minimum n achieving 80% power:", n_min, "participants\n")
cat("Power at n =", n_min, ":", round(power_min, 6), "\n")
cat("Power at n =", n_min - 1, ":", round(power_prev, 6), "\n\n")

# Verify calculation with closed-form approximation
# For reference: Wallis (2009) approximation for one-sample t-test
# n ≈ (z_{1-α} + z_{1-β})^2 / d^2 + d^2 / 4
z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha)  # one-sided
z_beta <- qnorm(target_power)
n_approx_wallis <- (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 / cohens_d^2 + cohens_d^2 / 4

cat("Closed-form approximation (Wallis):\n")
cat("n_approx ≈", round(n_approx_wallis, 2), "\n\n")

# Output for submission
cat("FINAL ANSWER:\n")
cat("Minimum integer sample size: n =", n_min, "participants\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", n_min, ":", round(power_min, 6), "\n")

# Emit structured result
results <- list(
  metric = "sample_size",
  value = n_min,
  unit = "participants_total"
)

library(jsonlite)
cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(toJSON(list(results = list(results)), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))
cat("\n")
